title: Diagnostic process inspection
intro: Selected design awaiting review and implementation. Dark Start here nodes mark graph entry; sequence diagrams begin at their first message. The historical acceptance result remains 0/10, unavailable.

groups.title: Ownership
groups.description: Keep target signal authority and reaping with one owner.

groups.title: Deadlines
groups.description: An inspection timeout fails evidence while safety actions continue.

groups.title: Helper creation
groups.description: Track helper ownership before exec without making teardown wait.

discussion.title: Keep inspection off the teardown path
discussion.summary: One prestarted read-only worker owns ps creation and waits. The outer controller owns workload signals and reaping. A failed worker is retired without replacement; teardown continues with uncertainty retained. Storage isolation remains a separate prerequisite.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Assigned target signals and reap to the controller, and helper mechanics to a read-only worker.
Made KILL independent of snapshot completion and closed target authority before reap.
Added creation intent, registered helper identity and a deadline-checked exec gate.

diagrams.title: Keep signals with the controller
diagrams.caption: Local process ownership. The worker may signal only its own unreaped direct helper; it never signals the workload. Both group leaders remain pinned until their group signal authority closes. Storage isolation is still unimplemented.

diagrams.title: Expire evidence without delaying safety
diagrams.caption: Delayed-inspection failure path for group termination. PID-only interruption keeps PID-only signals and skips KILL after leader exit. R is a time allocation inside K, not a ps latency guarantee. OS scheduling limits apply.

diagrams.title: Register before exec
diagrams.caption: Registration is in memory. A creation race can leave an unknown helper, which remains a failed residual. An acknowledged child scheduled after expiry is still invalid evidence; the gate is not an atomic scheduling guarantee.
